reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a PancakeSwap front-running bot while claiming it can earn 10 BNB daily and generate around 15x returns. It directs viewers to connect a wallet, deploy a supplied contract, deposit BNB, and activate the bot, tying the promised returns to a concrete cryptocurrency transfer flow. It also states that recovering deposited funds requires another BNB transfer.

citations.quote: How to EARN 10 BNB EVERY DAY
Deposit funds to exact your BOT contract address
After your transaction was confirmed, Start the BOT by clicking the "Action" button
the current Bot v2 with 1.0 BNB deposit earns up to 250~300% better return than the old Bot v1 generation
so we recommend you fund your BNB deposit to 1.0 BNB

opening.argument: Judge, the description does not present the contract as risk-free. It warns viewers that other contracts may imitate the bot and advises precautions for the safety of funds. It also addresses what to do if the contract generates no revenue, including the stated option to withdraw rather than add more. Those cautions deserve weight alongside the earnings claims: they leave room for a reading of the video as a risky technical walkthrough, not a promise that every viewer will profit.

citations.quote: If you are fooled by other contracts that imitate my clip robot, for the safety of funds, it is best to create a new wallet and delete the browser browsing history (cookie) before using the code
What should I do if there is no revenue generated after the contract runs?
You can choose to refer to Q1 to withdraw funds or add at least 1 BNB.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited daily-earnings headline and return comparison are claims, not proof that those returns occurred. The opening also omits the description's warning about imitating contracts and its acknowledgment that revenue may not appear. Funding and activating a contract are part of the demonstrated workflow, but those steps alone do not establish that the creator intends to deceive viewers.

citations.quote: If you are fooled by other contracts that imitate my clip robot, for the safety of funds
What should I do if there is no revenue generated after the contract runs?

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cautions do not change the transaction the viewer is asked to make. The description recommends a 1.0 BNB deposit to improve returns, then says recovering an earlier 1.0 BNB deposit requires transferring another 1.0 BNB plus a fee before executing the action. A warning about imitators does not make that additional-payment instruction benign.

citations.quote: so we recommend you fund your BNB deposit to 1.0 BNB to ensure competition with other active bots.
when you need to return the funds, you need to transfer 1.0 BNB to the contract, and then action

opening.argument: Judge, much of the video is an operational walkthrough. The speaker describes creating a contract file, compiling it, connecting a wallet to Remix, and checking the deployed address on a chain explorer. The description likewise gives concrete compiler and deployment settings. That technical sequence supports reading the video as a demonstration of a purported bot. The speaker's reported result should not be treated as independently verified, but an unverified result does not by itself settle whether the primary purpose is instruction or solicitation.

citations.quote: Under contracts I'm going to create a new contract which is with this Create New File icon on the top left.
There we go, it compiled. So we're going to deploy this to our wallet.
I copied that, paste it in BSC scan. You can see that there's an address there now.
select version "0.6.6" and then "Compile" it

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats the deployment steps as evidence of a scam, but those same steps are the subject of the spoken demonstration. A compiled contract and a visible address do not verify the claimed returns; equally, the absence of independent verification does not show that the walkthrough is deceptive. The speaker presents the action as part of explaining how the purported automation works.

citations.quote: we're going to see how the contract works
the action button then engages all the constructors that i built in as far as engaging the pancake router

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial format is precisely how viewers are directed into the funded-contract flow. The instructions say to paste supplied code, deposit funds to the contract address, and press Action; the title ties that workflow to daily BNB earnings. Showing compilation and deployment does not establish that the contract performs the claimed trading or that viewers can recover their funds.

citations.quote: Paste SmartContract in Remix: (Copy and Paste as it is)
Deposit funds to exact your BOT contract address
Start the BOT by clicking the "Action" button
How to EARN 10 BNB EVERY DAY

opening.argument: Judge, the funding instruction is real, but it says to send funds to the viewer's newly deployed contract, described as 'your own BOT.' The speaker also tells viewers to check that contract's address on BSC Scan. The supplied material does not establish who ultimately controls the contract's funds, whether the code diverts them, or whether the reported trading results occurred. Those are important missing facts before treating this as a demonstrated theft mechanism; the visible pitch can instead be read as promotion of a self-deployed trading tool.

citations.quote: After the transaction is confirmed, it's your own BOT now
Deposit funds to exact your BOT contract address
I copied that, paste it in BSC scan. You can see that there's an address there now.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening correctly identifies a deposit and an additional-transfer instruction, but it does not establish from those quotes where the contract sends funds or who can withdraw them. The description characterizes the destination as the viewer's own deployed contract. That claim warrants scrutiny, yet the cited instructions alone do not resolve the contract's actual behavior.

citations.quote: After the transaction is confirmed, it's your own BOT now
Transfer 0.0001bnb [as transfer fee] + previously transferred funds BNB to the previously deployed contract, and then execute the action.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling it 'your own BOT' does not establish control over code copied from a supplied link. The description instructs viewers to paste that code, fund the deployed address, and send the amount of their earlier deposit again to obtain a refund. A proven diversion of funds is not needed to recognize the promoted mechanism: promised trading returns are tied to funding a contract, with a further payment prescribed for recovery.
